english.quote: The medium of instruction in the Institute is English.
english.how_found: Searched the UG admissions, undergraduate, B.Tech, CSE B.Tech and Courses of Study (General/UG rules) pages for English test requirements.
english.notes: None of the reachable IIT Delhi pages give an English test minimum for UG foreign nationals, and none says that no test is required. The quote only confirms the teaching language. Admission is through JEE (Advanced); foreign-national eligibility is set by JEE (Advanced), on pages I could not reach (intladm.iitd.ac.in had a TLS error / HTTP 503, jeeadv.iitd.ac.in and international.iitd.ac.in were blocked or timed out). I did not mark this not_applicable because no IIT Delhi page I could read says so.

value.description: Admission to IIT Delhi B.Tech programmes, including for foreign nationals, is through JEE (Advanced) rank. No minimum school score was found on reachable IIT Delhi pages.

gpa.quote: Admission to the undergraduate programs at IIT Delhi is through the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Advanced, which follows the JEE Main examination.
gpa.notes: Route: foreign nationals are admitted through JEE (Advanced) (IIT JEE route, then JoSAA seat allocation), not DASA; DASA does not cover IITs, though no IIT Delhi page I could read says this in so many words. The home.iitd.ac.in Admissions menu links 'JEE (Advanced)' to https://jeeadv.iitd.ac.in/, and its 'Foreign Nationals' link (intladm.iitd.ac.in) is commented out in the HTML. Neither site was reachable. The search snippet for intladm.iitd.ac.in/eligibility-criteria.php reads 'For Eligibility of Undergraduate programmes refer to JEE Advanced', but I could not check it against the page. The UG Admissions page confirms the 2026 entrants were 'admitted through JEE (Advanced) 2026'. Rules like the JEE-Main exemption for foreign nationals, the 75% Class XII criterion and the age limit are on jeeadv.ac.in pages I did not reach; I recorded none of them. The CSE page says: 'We attract the brightest students from the country who score very high ranks in the IIT-JEE'.

deadline.how_found: Looked for JEE (Advanced) 2026/2027 foreign-national registration dates on iitd.ac.in pages and in a site-restricted search.
deadline.notes: The deadline that matters is the JEE (Advanced) registration deadline for foreign nationals (with JoSAA dates after it). It is published on the JEE (Advanced) portal (jeeadv.iitd.ac.in from the IIT Delhi menu was blocked by the egress proxy), not on any reachable IIT Delhi page. No 2027 or 2026 date was found on iitd.ac.in. The foreign-national deadlines that turned up (30 March 2026; 29.10.2026) are PG/PhD and do not apply.

tuition.quote: NON-SAARC USD 2OOO Rs 8150 + Rs 6250 + Rs 8000 + Rs 8600 = Rs 31,000 USD 2000 + Rs. 31,000
tuition.how_found: Site-restricted search for IIT Delhi UG fee for foreign nationals -> Academic Section circular 'fee structure for new entry students admitted to the Undergraduate Programmes ... for the Academic Year 2026-27' (academics.iitd.ac.in PDF).
tuition.notes: The quote is the PDF's OCR text layer copied exactly ('2OOO' with letter O is how the OCR reads it; the same row's total says 'USD 2000'). Tuition is USD 2,000. On top of that is INR 31,000: one-time 8,150 + other charges 6,250 + refundable caution deposit 8,000 + hostel seat rent 8,600. SAARC nationals pay USD 1,000. The document does not label the period explicitly. It is the fee due at registration, and it says '**Extra payment witt be adjusted in the next semester's fee.' (OCR), which fits a per-semester fee; not confirmed for an annual figure. No 2027-28 schedule is published. The 2025-26 schedule (https://academics.iitd.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Fee-Structure_2025-26_UG-Entry-Students-revised.pdf) has the same figures: 'NON-SAARC Countries $ 2000 Rs. 22,400 + Rs 8,600 = Rs 31,000 USD 2000 + Rs. 31,000'.

scholarship_exists.quote: The Institute offers Merit-cum-Means scholarships to undergraduate students in engineering and technology and students of M.A., M.Sc. and M.P.P. Programmes. These scholarships are offered to about 25% of the students whose annual family income is upto Rs. 8 lakh.
scholarship_exists.how_found: academics.iitd.ac.in -> Financial Assistance page; plus the linked donor-scholarships list (academics.iitd.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/scholarships.pdf), searched for nationality terms.
scholarship_exists.notes: Institute-run UG awards exist: Merit-cum-Means (MCM), Institute Free Studentship, SC/ST/PwD waivers and donor scholarships. None of them says whether foreign nationals can apply, and the criteria are Indian family income in Rs and JEE rank. The 2026-27 fee circular's income-based fee-concession note is a separate Indian tuition-slab mechanism. I found no named UG scholarship or waiver for foreign nationals. I did not mark this not_applicable because no page says outright that none exists, and the international office pages could not be reached.

scholarship_international.how_found: Read the Financial Assistance page and the donor scholarship PDF; no sentence on foreign-national eligibility.
scholarship_international.notes: No reachable official sentence says whether foreign undergraduates are eligible for, or excluded from, MCM or other institute scholarships.
